q1_issues.issue: The frequency adverb "always" in "the village always keeps the Stilllight Lantern lit" is dropped with no record at all — no QuantifierPhrase companion and no strength effect — so the sealed clause is indistinguishable from an unqualified "the village keeps the lantern lit".

q2_gaps: Frequency adverb on a habitual whose subject is a definite individual rather than a kind: the companion is specified as (QuantifierPhrase <kind> <verb-lemma> "<word>"), and there is no kind here; inside an attitude seal there is also no truth value for the frequency dial to set.

A day-of-year date ("day 68 of Year 1", no month): the calendar terms define (Day n) at day-of-month granularity, and the seeded date-ordering rules key on year/month/day, so (Day 68)+(Year 1) is representable but not interpretable as stated.
notes: Everything else checks out: tell/write route as non-factive attitudes (Experiencer holder, Recipient addressee, sealed Theme) with only definite/named typing and compound-genus atoms projected, the two generic complements become distributing rules with the adjectival restriction as a premise conjunct, and "keeps ... lit" uses the maintenance State-result shape with Result + Still + the flat atom kept inside the seal. The sealed rules' generic 0.9 strength is unexpressible inside a seal — the registered in-seal limitation, not a parse choice.
